First thanks xlogicx for directing me here. So yesterday I installed VIrtualBox on my 8.1 Pro machine, I converted my old Win 7 img to vdmk, and attempted to create a new VM. Unfortunately I was missing all the 64 bit options from the VM creation drop down. So I went into my BIOS and enabled VT-d, reboot and still no x64 option, so I did a little digging and came across a solution or so I thought that specified that I need to disable Hyper-V in the OS via command line. I used the following two commands:

bcdedit /set hypervisorlaunchtype off
dism.exe /Online /Disable-Feature:Microsoft-Hyper-V

I rebooted and still no x64 option for the VMs Any ideas?

EDIT: Figured it out. Apparently there are two spots in the Asus Rampage V Extreme BIOS where virtualization needs to be enabled. Under Advanced - CPU "Enable Virtualization" and under Advanced - System Agent "Enable VT-x"
VirtualBox in Windows 8.1 will not allow x64 VMs.
I think it has something to do with hardware virtualisation (Ctrl+F intel). Although that documentation says to enable it, try disabling it to see what happens.
Never had any of these issues on my AMD cpu, ugh, this is turning out to be a nuisance. Thanks though, I'll do more digging this weekend and try and fix the problem.
OK, Im pretty sure I had a similar issue to you a while back with my Intel CPU, I think turning off the virtualisation of in the BIOS fixed it for me.
Yes I have, I turned off Hyper-V and turned on VT-x in the BIOS. I still can not run x64 VMs.

Running those bcdedit & dism.exe commands should only effect the ability to use VirtualBox or Hyper-V. If you can already create even a 32bit machine in VirtualBox, you shouldn't need to do this.
I've run in to this issue before and resolved it by enabling the virtualization technology option in the BIOS.

Since it seems as thought you've done the above, I'd check these possible fixes:
After changing the virtualization technology option, VirtualBox may need to be reinstalled for the x64bit option to appear.
A restart may not be sufficient. A full power down may be required after changing the virtualization technology option in the BIOS.
Thanks, I was thinking I might need to reinstall as perhaps it hard codes during install weather or not VT-x is present on the system.
Did you manage to get the issue resolved?
Yes I did, have a look at my edit in the OP post. There were two areas where I had to enable virtualization.
